    def _check_conv_with_multidim_outputs(self, f: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Raise if the model has a conv layer and the outputs have more than one
    batch dim, e.g. `(B, H, W, K)` with one prediction per pixel.

    For such outputs, the KFAC input factor that ASDL computes for a conv layer
    is \\( H W \\) times smaller than the one from Curvlinops, or from the same
    net written with `nn.Linear` layers applied to every pixel. Outputs
    `(B, K)`, e.g. after global pooling, are not affected. ASDL is no longer
    maintained, so we raise instead of patching it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        The model outputs, with the output dim last.

    Raises
    ------
    NotImplementedError
        If `f` has more than two dims and the model has a trainable conv layer.
    """
    if f.ndim <= 2:
        return

    convs = (
        nn.Conv1d,
        nn.Conv2d,
        nn.Conv3d,
        nn.ConvTranspose1d,
        nn.ConvTranspose2d,
        nn.ConvTranspose3d,
    )
    has_conv = any(
        isinstance(module, convs)
        and any(p.requires_grad for p in module.parameters())
        for module in self._model.modules()
    )

    if has_conv:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "ASDL computes wrong Kronecker factors for conv layers when the "
            "outputs have more than one batch dim, here outputs of shape "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)}. Use a "
            "Curvlinops backend (`CurvlinopsGGN` or `CurvlinopsEF`) instead."
        )

    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore a pickled backend.

    Pickles made before likelihood objects existed store the likelihood as a
    string under `likelihood`. It is turned into a likelihood object here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : dict[str, Any]
        the pickled `__dict__`.
    """
    state = dict(state)

    if "likelihood" in state:
        state["_likelihood"] = get_likelihood(state.pop("likelihood"))

    self.__dict__.pop("likelihood", None)
    self.__dict__.update(state)

    def _honours(self, method: str, y: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the library of this backend computes the curvature of `method`
    for the likelihood exactly.

    That is the case if the likelihood is exactly one of the `_library_types`,
    e.g. a `GaussianLikelihood` or a `CategoricalLikelihood`, whose losses the
    libraries know, and the library implements all of its non-default options. A
    subclass might override any member, e.g. `output_hessian`, which the library
    cannot see.

    With the targets `y`, the option `ignore_index` also counts as set if `y`
    holds ignored positions, even with the default `-100`. Libraries that don't
    honour it would count those positions, e.g. padding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"diag"`, `"kron"`, or `"full"`.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch.

    Returns
    -------
    honours : bool
    """
    if type(self.likelihood) not in self._library_types:
        return False

    options = set(self.likelihood.hyperparameters())

    if y is not None and _ignored_positions(self.likelihood, y) > 0:
        options.add("ignore_index")

    return options <= self._honoured_options(method)

    def _unsupported_error(
    self,
    method: str,
    honoured: frozenset[str] | None = None,
    stochastic: bool = False,
    y: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> ValueError:
    """Error for a curvature method that cannot handle the likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"kron"`.
    honoured : frozenset[str], optional
        options that the method honours, `_honoured_options(method)` by
        default.
    stochastic : bool, default=False
        whether the method computes a Monte Carlo Fisher.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch. If they hold ignored positions, `ignore_index`
        counts as an option, as in `_honours`.

    Returns
    -------
    error : ValueError
    """
    likelihood = self.likelihood

    if type(likelihood) in self._library_types:
        if honoured is None:
            honoured = self._honoured_options(method)

        options = set(likelihood.hyperparameters())

        if y is not None and _ignored_positions(likelihood, y) > 0:
            options.add("ignore_index")

        options = sorted(options - honoured)
        noun = "options" if len(options) > 1 else "option"
        what = f"the {noun} {', '.join(options)} of {likelihood!r}"
    else:
        what = f"the likelihood {likelihood!r}"

    where = f"{type(self).__name__}.{method}"

    if stochastic:
        where += " with stochastic=True"

    return ValueError(
        f"{where} does not support {what}. Use a deterministic GGN or EF "
        f"backend with the `diag` or `full` structure, which support any "
        f"likelihood."
    )

    def _check_backward_hooks(self, full: bool) -> None:
    """Check that the model takes the kind of backward hooks the library uses.

    PyTorch refuses a module both regular and full backward hooks, and it
    remembers the kind of a hook after the hook is removed. ASDL registers
    regular hooks and leaves that mark on the model. BackPACK registers full
    ones, but its backends remove them and the mark after each computation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    full : bool
        whether the library registers full backward hooks.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        if a module of the model already had the other kind of backward hook.
    """
    clash = not full  # the flag PyTorch keeps for the other kind

    if not any(
        getattr(module, "_is_full_backward_hook", None) is clash
        for module in self._model.modules()
    ):
        return

    if full:
        what = "regular backward hooks, e.g. from fitting an ASDL backend"
    else:
        what = "full backward hooks, from `register_full_backward_hook`"

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"{type(self).__name__} can't use a model that had {what}. PyTorch "
        f"doesn't allow both kinds of backward hooks on one module, and it "
        f"remembers the kind after a hook is removed. Use a Curvlinops backend, "
        f"or a fresh instance of the model with the same weights, loaded with "
        f"`load_state_dict`."
    )

    def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_\\theta f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using asdfghjkl's gradient per output dimension.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping (e.g. dict, UserDict)
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model if torch.Tensor.
        If MutableMapping, then at least contains `self.dict_key_x`.
        The latter is specific for reward modeling.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `([batch_dims], outputs, parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `([batch_dims], outputs)`
    """
    Js = list()
    # `self.model.output_size` can be stale, e.g. in reward modeling where the
    # output size differs between fitting and prediction. So, get the number of
    # outputs from the first forward pass instead.
    n_outputs = 1
    i = 0
    while i < n_outputs:

        def closure():
            self.model.zero_grad()
            f = self.model(x)
            loss = f[..., i].sum()
            loss.backward(
                create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
            )
            return f

        Ji, f = self._batch_gradient(closure)
        n_outputs = f.shape[-1]

        if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
            Ji = Ji[:, self.subnetwork_indices]

        Js.append(Ji)
        i += 1

    Js = torch.stack(Js, dim=1)  # (n_rows, n_outputs, n_params)

    # ASDL returns one row per row of the layers' inputs, e.g. per position. Sum those
    # belonging to the same observation, e.g. when the outputs are pooled over positions.
    n_obs = f.shape[:-1].numel()
    Js = self._sum_rows_per_observation(Js, n_obs)

    if Js.shape[0] == n_obs:
        # Restore the individual batch dims of the outputs
        Js = Js.reshape(*f.shape[:-1], *Js.shape[-2:])

    return Js, f

    def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

    def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute parameter Jacobians for selected output coordinates per input.

    The default computes all output Jacobians before selecting coordinates.
    Backends may override it to avoid materializing the full Jacobian.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        Input data on the model's device, with a leading batch dimension.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    # Use the output shape observed at this input. Reward models return two
    # training logits but one output for an individual inference input.
    jacobians, values = CurvatureInterface.jacobians(
        self, x, enable_backprop=enable_backprop
    )

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != jacobians.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    selected = torch.gather(
        jacobians,
        dim=1,
        index=outputs.to(jacobians.device, dtype=torch.long)
        .unsqueeze(-1)
        .expand(-1, -1, jacobians.shape[-1]),
    )

    return selected, values

    def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at current parameter
    \\(\\theta\\) using asdfghjkl's backend.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    loss : torch.Tensor
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(n_observations, parameters)`
    """

    # With `last_layer`, `self._model` is the last layer. Map the inputs to the
    # features, so that the gradients are those of the last layer's parameters only.
    if self.last_layer:
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, x = self.model.forward_with_features(x)

    f = None

    def closure():
        nonlocal f
        self._model.zero_grad()
        f = self._model(x)
        loss = self._loss(f, y)
        loss.backward()
        return loss

    Gs, loss = self._batch_gradient(closure, self._model)

    # The last dim of the outputs is the output dim
    n_obs = f.shape[:-1].numel()
    Gs = self._sum_rows_per_observation(Gs, n_obs)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
    return Gs, loss

    def _flatten_targets(self, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Flatten the targets to match the logits that ASDL flattens to `(M, K)`.

    ASDL builds the model output lazily, so its shape is only known after the
    forward pass. As in `nn.CrossEntropyLoss`, the dtype tells class probabilities
    from class indices instead. `_check_targets` verifies the shape afterwards.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y : torch.Tensor
        targets of the batch. For classification, class indices
        `(batch, ...)` or class probabilities `(batch, ..., K)`.

    Returns
    -------
    y : torch.Tensor
        `y` itself for regression, else class probabilities `(M, K)` or class
        indices `(M,)`, where `M` is the number of positions.
    """
    if self.loss_type == LOSS_MSE:
        return y

    if y.is_floating_point():
        return y.reshape(-1, y.shape[-1])

    return y.reshape(-1)

    def _batch_gradient(
    self, closure: Callable[[], Any], model: nn.Module | None = None
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, Any]:
    """ASDL's `batch_gradient` with a clearer error for models whose layers have
    different numbers of gradient rows, e.g., position-wise layers followed by a
    head applied after pooling over positions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    closure : Callable
        Runs the forward and backward pass of `model`.
    model : nn.Module, optional
        The module whose parameters get gradients. Defaults to `self.model`.
    """
    model = self.model if model is None else model
    self._check_backward_hooks(full=False)

    try:
        return batch_gradient(model, closure, return_outputs=True)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        if "Sizes of tensors must match" not in str(e):
            raise
        raise RuntimeError(
            "ASDL returned different numbers of gradient rows for different layers, "
            "e.g., for outputs pooled over positions. Use a Curvlinops backend "
            "(`CurvlinopsGGN` or `CurvlinopsEF`) for such models."
        ) from e

    @staticmethod
def _sum_rows_per_observation(A: torch.Tensor, n_obs: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """ASDL returns one row per row of the layers' inputs (e.g. per position), but
    an observation can span several of them (e.g. pooled outputs, or pairs in
    reward modeling). Sum the rows that belong to the same observation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    A : torch.Tensor
        `(n_rows, ...)`, where rows of the same observation are consecutive.
    n_obs : int
        number of observations, i.e., product of the leading dims of the outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    A : torch.Tensor
        `(n_obs, ...)`

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        if `n_rows` is not a multiple of `n_obs`.
    """
    n_rows = A.shape[0]
    if n_rows == n_obs:
        return A
    if n_obs == 0 or n_rows % n_obs != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"ASDL returned {n_rows} per-example rows, which cannot be grouped "
            f"into {n_obs} observations (the leading dims of the outputs)."
        )
    return A.reshape(n_obs, n_rows // n_obs, *A.shape[1:]).sum(1)

    def _get_kron_factors(
    self,
    M: int,
    input_factors: dict[nn.Module, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
) -> Kron:
    """Collect the Kronecker factors that ASDL stored on the modules.

    Parameters
    ----------
    M : int
        number of positions in the batch that count as observations.
    input_factors : dict[nn.Module, torch.Tensor], optional
        input factors that replace those of ASDL, from
        `_observed_input_factors`.

    Returns
    -------
    kron : Kron
    """
    kfacs = list()
    for module in self.model.modules():
        if _is_batchnorm(module):
            warnings.warn("BatchNorm unsupported for Kron, ignore.")
            continue

        stats = getattr(module, "fisher", None)
        if stats is None:
            continue

        B = stats.kron.B

        if input_factors is None:
            A = stats.kron.A
        else:
            # ASDL's factors are sums over the positions, and
            # `_rescale_kron_factors` divides them by the number of data. So scale
            # the mean by the number `M` of observed positions.
            A = input_factors[module] * M

        if hasattr(module, "bias") and module.bias is not None:
            # split up bias and weights
            kfacs.append([B, A])
            kfacs.append([B])
        elif hasattr(module, "weight"):
            p, q = B.numel(), A.numel()
            if p == q == 1:
                kfacs.append([B * A])
            else:
                kfacs.append([B, A])
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Whats happening with {module}?")
    return Kron(kfacs)

    def _check_conv_with_multidim_outputs(self, f: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Raise if the model has a conv layer and the outputs have more than one
    batch dim, e.g. `(B, H, W, K)` with one prediction per pixel.

    For such outputs, the KFAC input factor that ASDL computes for a conv layer
    is \\( H W \\) times smaller than the one from Curvlinops, or from the same
    net written with `nn.Linear` layers applied to every pixel. Outputs
    `(B, K)`, e.g. after global pooling, are not affected. ASDL is no longer
    maintained, so we raise instead of patching it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        The model outputs, with the output dim last.

    Raises
    ------
    NotImplementedError
        If `f` has more than two dims and the model has a trainable conv layer.
    """
    if f.ndim <= 2:
        return

    convs = (
        nn.Conv1d,
        nn.Conv2d,
        nn.Conv3d,
        nn.ConvTranspose1d,
        nn.ConvTranspose2d,
        nn.ConvTranspose3d,
    )
    has_conv = any(
        isinstance(module, convs)
        and any(p.requires_grad for p in module.parameters())
        for module in self._model.modules()
    )

    if has_conv:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "ASDL computes wrong Kronecker factors for conv layers when the "
            "outputs have more than one batch dim, here outputs of shape "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)}. Use a "
            "Curvlinops backend (`CurvlinopsGGN` or `CurvlinopsEF`) instead."
        )

    def full(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if not self._honours("full"):
        raise self._unsupported_error("full")

    if self.last_layer:
        _, x = self.model.forward_with_features(x)

    cfg = HessianConfig(hessian_shapes=[SHAPE_FULL])
    # With `last_layer`, `x` are the features and `self._model` the last layer
    hess_maker = HessianMaker(self._model, cfg)

    dummy = hess_maker.setup_model_call(self._model, x)
    dummy = (
        dummy if self.loss_type == LOSS_MSE else dummy.reshape(-1, dummy.size(-1))
    )
    y = self._flatten_targets(y)

    hess_maker.setup_loss_call(self.lossfunc, dummy, y)
    hess_maker.forward_and_backward()

    H = self._model.hessian.data
    f = self._model(x).detach()
    # Assumes that the last dimension of f is of size outputs.
    f = f if self.loss_type == LOSS_MSE else f.reshape(-1, f.size(-1))
    loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)

    return self.factor * loss, self.factor * H

    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore a pickled backend.

    Pickles made before likelihood objects existed store the likelihood as a
    string under `likelihood`. It is turned into a likelihood object here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : dict[str, Any]
        the pickled `__dict__`.
    """
    state = dict(state)

    if "likelihood" in state:
        state["_likelihood"] = get_likelihood(state.pop("likelihood"))

    self.__dict__.pop("likelihood", None)
    self.__dict__.update(state)

    def _honours(self, method: str, y: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the library of this backend computes the curvature of `method`
    for the likelihood exactly.

    That is the case if the likelihood is exactly one of the `_library_types`,
    e.g. a `GaussianLikelihood` or a `CategoricalLikelihood`, whose losses the
    libraries know, and the library implements all of its non-default options. A
    subclass might override any member, e.g. `output_hessian`, which the library
    cannot see.

    With the targets `y`, the option `ignore_index` also counts as set if `y`
    holds ignored positions, even with the default `-100`. Libraries that don't
    honour it would count those positions, e.g. padding.

    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"diag"`, `"kron"`, or `"full"`.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch.

    Returns
    -------
    honours : bool
    """
    if type(self.likelihood) not in self._library_types:
        return False

    options = set(self.likelihood.hyperparameters())

    if y is not None and _ignored_positions(self.likelihood, y) > 0:
        options.add("ignore_index")

    return options <= self._honoured_options(method)

    def _unsupported_error(
    self,
    method: str,
    honoured: frozenset[str] | None = None,
    stochastic: bool = False,
    y: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> ValueError:
    """Error for a curvature method that cannot handle the likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"kron"`.
    honoured : frozenset[str], optional
        options that the method honours, `_honoured_options(method)` by
        default.
    stochastic : bool, default=False
        whether the method computes a Monte Carlo Fisher.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch. If they hold ignored positions, `ignore_index`
        counts as an option, as in `_honours`.

    Returns
    -------
    error : ValueError
    """
    likelihood = self.likelihood

    if type(likelihood) in self._library_types:
        if honoured is None:
            honoured = self._honoured_options(method)

        options = set(likelihood.hyperparameters())

        if y is not None and _ignored_positions(likelihood, y) > 0:
            options.add("ignore_index")

        options = sorted(options - honoured)
        noun = "options" if len(options) > 1 else "option"
        what = f"the {noun} {', '.join(options)} of {likelihood!r}"
    else:
        what = f"the likelihood {likelihood!r}"

    where = f"{type(self).__name__}.{method}"

    if stochastic:
        where += " with stochastic=True"

    return ValueError(
        f"{where} does not support {what}. Use a deterministic GGN or EF "
        f"backend with the `diag` or `full` structure, which support any "
        f"likelihood."
    )

    def _check_backward_hooks(self, full: bool) -> None:
    """Check that the model takes the kind of backward hooks the library uses.

    PyTorch refuses a module both regular and full backward hooks, and it
    remembers the kind of a hook after the hook is removed. ASDL registers
    regular hooks and leaves that mark on the model. BackPACK registers full
    ones, but its backends remove them and the mark after each computation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    full : bool
        whether the library registers full backward hooks.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        if a module of the model already had the other kind of backward hook.
    """
    clash = not full  # the flag PyTorch keeps for the other kind

    if not any(
        getattr(module, "_is_full_backward_hook", None) is clash
        for module in self._model.modules()
    ):
        return

    if full:
        what = "regular backward hooks, e.g. from fitting an ASDL backend"
    else:
        what = "full backward hooks, from `register_full_backward_hook`"

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"{type(self).__name__} can't use a model that had {what}. PyTorch "
        f"doesn't allow both kinds of backward hooks on one module, and it "
        f"remembers the kind after a hook is removed. Use a Curvlinops backend, "
        f"or a fresh instance of the model with the same weights, loaded with "
        f"`load_state_dict`."
    )

    def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

    _extended(module: Module | None = None) -> Iterator[Module]

    Extend module and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break torch.func and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind. Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    @contextmanager
def _extended(self, module: nn.Module | None = None) -> Iterator[nn.Module]:
    """Extend `module` and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break
    `torch.func` and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added
    here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind.
    Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK
    checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback
    decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    Parameters
    ----------
    module : nn.Module, optional
        module to extend, `self._model` by default.

    Yields
    ------
    module : nn.Module
        the extended module.
    """
    module = self._model if module is None else module
    self._check_backward_hooks(full=True)

    modules = list(module.modules())
    kinds = [m._is_full_backward_hook for m in modules]
    lossfunc = (
        self.lossfunc if type(self.likelihood) in self._library_types else None
    )

    try:
        extend(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            extend(lossfunc)

        yield module
    finally:
        CTX.remove_hooks()
        _cleanup(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            _cleanup(lossfunc)

        for m, kind in zip(modules, kinds):
            m._is_full_backward_hook = kind

        probabilities, see `_flatten_categorical_targets`.

    def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using backpack's BatchGrad per output dimension. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, parameters, outputs)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        to_stack = []
        for i in range(model.output_size):
            model.zero_grad()
            out = model(x)
            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                if model.output_size > 1:
                    out[:, i].sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                else:
                    out.sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                to_cat = []
                for param in model.parameters():
                    to_cat.append(param.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1))
                    delattr(param, "grad_batch")
                Jk = torch.cat(to_cat, dim=1)
                if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
                    Jk = Jk[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
            to_stack.append(Jk)
            if i == 0:
                f = out

        model.zero_grad()

    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad

    if model.output_size > 1:
        J = torch.stack(to_stack, dim=2).transpose(1, 2)
    else:
        J = Jk.unsqueeze(-1).transpose(1, 2)

    return (J, f) if enable_backprop else (J.detach(), f.detach())

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch, parameters)`
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    with self._extended():
        f = self.model(x)
        loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            loss.backward()
    Gs = torch.cat(
        [p.grad_batch.data.flatten(start_dim=1) for p in self._model.parameters()],
        dim=1,
    )
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
    return Gs, loss

    def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute selected output Jacobians using BackPACK's BatchGrad.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input data of shape `(batch, input_shape)` on the model's device.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        columns = []
        first_output = None

        for column in range(outputs.shape[1]):
            model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            output = model(x)
            if first_output is None:
                first_output = output

            selected = output.gather(
                1, outputs[:, column : column + 1].to(output.device)
            ).sum()

            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                selected.backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
                columns.append(
                    torch.cat(
                        [
                            parameter.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
                            for parameter in model.parameters()
                            if parameter.requires_grad
                        ],
                        dim=1,
                    )
                )
                for parameter in model.parameters():
                    if hasattr(parameter, "grad_batch"):
                        delattr(parameter, "grad_batch")

        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
            x.grad = input_grad

    result = torch.stack(columns, dim=1)
    assert first_output is not None

    return (
        (result, first_output)
        if enable_backprop
        else (
            result.detach(),
            first_output.detach(),
        )
    )

    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore a pickled backend.

    Pickles made before likelihood objects existed store the likelihood as a
    string under `likelihood`. It is turned into a likelihood object here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : dict[str, Any]
        the pickled `__dict__`.
    """
    state = dict(state)

    if "likelihood" in state:
        state["_likelihood"] = get_likelihood(state.pop("likelihood"))

    self.__dict__.pop("likelihood", None)
    self.__dict__.update(state)

    def _honours(self, method: str, y: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the library of this backend computes the curvature of `method`
    for the likelihood exactly.

    That is the case if the likelihood is exactly one of the `_library_types`,
    e.g. a `GaussianLikelihood` or a `CategoricalLikelihood`, whose losses the
    libraries know, and the library implements all of its non-default options. A
    subclass might override any member, e.g. `output_hessian`, which the library
    cannot see.

    With the targets `y`, the option `ignore_index` also counts as set if `y`
    holds ignored positions, even with the default `-100`. Libraries that don't
    honour it would count those positions, e.g. padding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"diag"`, `"kron"`, or `"full"`.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch.

    Returns
    -------
    honours : bool
    """
    if type(self.likelihood) not in self._library_types:
        return False

    options = set(self.likelihood.hyperparameters())

    if y is not None and _ignored_positions(self.likelihood, y) > 0:
        options.add("ignore_index")

    return options <= self._honoured_options(method)

    def _unsupported_error(
    self,
    method: str,
    honoured: frozenset[str] | None = None,
    stochastic: bool = False,
    y: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> ValueError:
    """Error for a curvature method that cannot handle the likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"kron"`.
    honoured : frozenset[str], optional
        options that the method honours, `_honoured_options(method)` by
        default.
    stochastic : bool, default=False
        whether the method computes a Monte Carlo Fisher.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch. If they hold ignored positions, `ignore_index`
        counts as an option, as in `_honours`.

    Returns
    -------
    error : ValueError
    """
    likelihood = self.likelihood

    if type(likelihood) in self._library_types:
        if honoured is None:
            honoured = self._honoured_options(method)

        options = set(likelihood.hyperparameters())

        if y is not None and _ignored_positions(likelihood, y) > 0:
            options.add("ignore_index")

        options = sorted(options - honoured)
        noun = "options" if len(options) > 1 else "option"
        what = f"the {noun} {', '.join(options)} of {likelihood!r}"
    else:
        what = f"the likelihood {likelihood!r}"

    where = f"{type(self).__name__}.{method}"

    if stochastic:
        where += " with stochastic=True"

    return ValueError(
        f"{where} does not support {what}. Use a deterministic GGN or EF "
        f"backend with the `diag` or `full` structure, which support any "
        f"likelihood."
    )

    def _check_backward_hooks(self, full: bool) -> None:
    """Check that the model takes the kind of backward hooks the library uses.

    PyTorch refuses a module both regular and full backward hooks, and it
    remembers the kind of a hook after the hook is removed. ASDL registers
    regular hooks and leaves that mark on the model. BackPACK registers full
    ones, but its backends remove them and the mark after each computation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    full : bool
        whether the library registers full backward hooks.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        if a module of the model already had the other kind of backward hook.
    """
    clash = not full  # the flag PyTorch keeps for the other kind

    if not any(
        getattr(module, "_is_full_backward_hook", None) is clash
        for module in self._model.modules()
    ):
        return

    if full:
        what = "regular backward hooks, e.g. from fitting an ASDL backend"
    else:
        what = "full backward hooks, from `register_full_backward_hook`"

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"{type(self).__name__} can't use a model that had {what}. PyTorch "
        f"doesn't allow both kinds of backward hooks on one module, and it "
        f"remembers the kind after a hook is removed. Use a Curvlinops backend, "
        f"or a fresh instance of the model with the same weights, loaded with "
        f"`load_state_dict`."
    )

    def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using backpack's BatchGrad per output dimension. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, parameters, outputs)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        to_stack = []
        for i in range(model.output_size):
            model.zero_grad()
            out = model(x)
            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                if model.output_size > 1:
                    out[:, i].sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                else:
                    out.sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                to_cat = []
                for param in model.parameters():
                    to_cat.append(param.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1))
                    delattr(param, "grad_batch")
                Jk = torch.cat(to_cat, dim=1)
                if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
                    Jk = Jk[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
            to_stack.append(Jk)
            if i == 0:
                f = out

        model.zero_grad()

    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad

    if model.output_size > 1:
        J = torch.stack(to_stack, dim=2).transpose(1, 2)
    else:
        J = Jk.unsqueeze(-1).transpose(1, 2)

    return (J, f) if enable_backprop else (J.detach(), f.detach())

    def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

    def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute selected output Jacobians using BackPACK's BatchGrad.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input data of shape `(batch, input_shape)` on the model's device.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        columns = []
        first_output = None

        for column in range(outputs.shape[1]):
            model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            output = model(x)
            if first_output is None:
                first_output = output

            selected = output.gather(
                1, outputs[:, column : column + 1].to(output.device)
            ).sum()

            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                selected.backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
                columns.append(
                    torch.cat(
                        [
                            parameter.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
                            for parameter in model.parameters()
                            if parameter.requires_grad
                        ],
                        dim=1,
                    )
                )
                for parameter in model.parameters():
                    if hasattr(parameter, "grad_batch"):
                        delattr(parameter, "grad_batch")

        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
            x.grad = input_grad

    result = torch.stack(columns, dim=1)
    assert first_output is not None

    return (
        (result, first_output)
        if enable_backprop
        else (
            result.detach(),
            first_output.detach(),
        )
    )

    def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at current parameter
    \\(\\theta\\) using Backpack's BatchGrad. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch, parameters)`
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    with self._extended():
        f = self.model(x)
        loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            loss.backward()
    Gs = torch.cat(
        [p.grad_batch.data.flatten(start_dim=1) for p in self._model.parameters()],
        dim=1,
    )
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
    return Gs, loss

    def full(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the full GGN \\(P \\times P\\) matrix as Hessian approximation
    \\(H_{ggn}\\) with respect to parameters \\(\\theta \\in \\mathbb{R}^P\\).
    For last-layer, reduced to \\(\\theta_{last}\\)

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)`
    y : torch.Tensor
        labels `(batch, label_shape)`

    Returns
    -------
    loss : torch.Tensor
    H : torch.Tensor
        GGN `(parameters, parameters)`
    """
    if self.stochastic:
        self._check_mc_fisher("full")

    Js, f = self.last_layer_jacobians(x) if self.last_layer else self.jacobians(x)
    H_lik = (
        self._get_mc_functional_fisher(f, y)
        if self.stochastic
        else self._get_functional_hessian(f, y)
    )

    if H_lik is not None:
        H = torch.einsum("...cp,...ck,...kq->pq", Js, H_lik, Js)
    else:  # The case of exact GGN for regression
        H = torch.einsum("...cp,...cq->pq", Js, Js)
    loss = self.factor * self._loss(f, y)

    return loss.detach(), H.detach()

Custom likelihoods are fine, since the sampled gradients estimate their Fisher. Positions with the default ignore index, e.g. padding, are masked with the observed targets.

    def _check_mc_fisher(self, method: str) -> None:
    """Make sure the Monte Carlo Fisher supports the likelihood.

    It draws targets from the likelihood and uses `output_gradient` at them. So
    it cannot see the observed targets, which class weights and ignored positions
    refer to. `output_gradient` would also smooth the sampled targets, which
    changes the expected outer product. Custom likelihoods are fine, since the
    sampled gradients estimate their Fisher. Positions with the default ignore
    index, e.g. padding, are masked with the observed targets.


    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, `"diag"` or `"full"`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        if the likelihood is a built-in one with non-default options.
    """
    # The samples and the output gradient of a Gaussian likelihood use its noise
    # std per output, so the sampled Fisher stays exact
    honoured = frozenset({"sigma_noise"})

    if (
        type(self.likelihood) in _BUILTIN_TYPES
        and set(self.likelihood.hyperparameters()) - honoured
    ):
        raise self._unsupported_error(method, honoured, stochastic=True)

    def _get_mc_functional_fisher(
    self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Approximate the Fisher's middle matrix (expected outer product of the functional gradient)
    using MC integral with `self.num_samples` many samples.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        model outputs `(batch, ..., outputs)`
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        observed targets. The positions that a categorical likelihood ignores in
        them, e.g. padding, get a zero Fisher.

    Returns
    -------
    F : torch.Tensor
        `(batch, ..., outputs, outputs)`
    """
    F = 0

    for _ in range(self.num_samples):
        y_sample = self.likelihood.sample(f)
        grad_sample = self.likelihood.output_gradient(f, y_sample)

        F += (
            1
            / self.num_samples
            * torch.einsum("...c,...k->...ck", grad_sample, grad_sample)
        )

    if y is not None and _ignored_positions(self.likelihood, y) > 0:
        mask = (y != self.likelihood.ignore_index).reshape(f.shape[:-1])
        F = mask[..., None, None] * F

    return F

    def _get_functional_hessian(
    self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """Hessian of the negative log likelihood w.r.t. the outputs `f`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        model outputs `(batch, ..., outputs)`
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets, passed on to the likelihood's `output_hessian`.

    Returns
    -------
    H : torch.Tensor or None
        `(batch, ..., outputs, outputs)`, or `None` for a Gaussian likelihood,
        whose output Hessian is the identity and is skipped in the GGN. With a
        noise std per output, the output Hessian is not the identity.
    """
    if self.likelihood.is_gaussian and _noise_per_output(self.likelihood) is None:
        return None

    return self.likelihood.output_hessian(f, y)

    _extended(module: Module | None = None) -> Iterator[Module]

    Extend module and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break torch.func and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind. Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    @contextmanager
def _extended(self, module: nn.Module | None = None) -> Iterator[nn.Module]:
    """Extend `module` and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break
    `torch.func` and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added
    here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind.
    Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK
    checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback
    decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    Parameters
    ----------
    module : nn.Module, optional
        module to extend, `self._model` by default.

    Yields
    ------
    module : nn.Module
        the extended module.
    """
    module = self._model if module is None else module
    self._check_backward_hooks(full=True)

    modules = list(module.modules())
    kinds = [m._is_full_backward_hook for m in modules]
    lossfunc = (
        self.lossfunc if type(self.likelihood) in self._library_types else None
    )

    try:
        extend(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            extend(lossfunc)

        yield module
    finally:
        CTX.remove_hooks()
        _cleanup(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            _cleanup(lossfunc)

        for m, kind in zip(modules, kinds):
            m._is_full_backward_hook = kind

    def _flatten_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Flatten the targets to match the logits that are flattened to `(M, K)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        outputs of the model for the batch, not flattened.
    y : torch.Tensor
        targets of the batch. For classification, class indices or class
        probabilities.

    Returns
    -------
    y : torch.Tensor

        probabilities, see `_flatten_categorical_targets`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        if the targets don't fit the outputs.

    if self.likelihood.name == Likelihood.REGRESSION.name:

    self._check_targets(f, y)

    return _flatten_categorical_targets(f, y)

    def diag(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if not self._honours("diag", y):
        return super().diag(x, y, **kwargs)

    context = DiagGGNMC if self.stochastic else DiagGGNExact
    with self._extended():
        f = self.model(x)
        y = self._flatten_targets(f, y)
        # Assumes that the last dimension of f is of size outputs.
        f = (
            f
            if self.likelihood.name == Likelihood.REGRESSION.name
            else f.view(-1, f.size(-1))
        )
        loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(context()):
            loss.backward()
    dggn = self._get_diag_ggn()
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        dggn = dggn[self.subnetwork_indices]

    return self.factor * loss.detach(), self.factor * dggn

    def kron(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    N: int,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, Kron]:
    if not self._honours("kron"):
        raise self._unsupported_error("kron")

    context = KFAC if self.stochastic else KFLR
    lossfunc = self.lossfunc
    mask = _observed_mask(self.likelihood, y)
    full_loss = None

    if mask is not None:
        # The loss counts the ignored positions as zero, so keep it from all
        # targets. The curvature is computed from the observed examples alone.
        with torch.no_grad():
            full_loss = self._loss(self.model(x), y)

        x, y = x[mask], y[mask]

    with self._extended():
        # BackPACK's loss raises for any `ignore_index` but the default one. A plain
        # loss does the same once the ignored positions are dropped, and it can't
        # zero a sampled label that equals `ignore_index`.
        if mask is not None or self._has_custom_ignore_index:
            lossfunc = extend(
                nn.CrossEntropyLoss(
                    reduction="sum", label_smoothing=self.likelihood.label_smoothing
                )
            )

        f = self.model(x)
        y = self._flatten_targets(f, y)
        # Assumes that the last dimension of f is of size outputs.
        f = (
            f
            if self.likelihood.name == Likelihood.REGRESSION.name
            else f.view(-1, f.size(-1))
        )
        loss = lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(context()):
            loss.backward()
    kron = self._get_kron_factors()
    kron = self._rescale_kron_factors(kron, len(y), N)

    if full_loss is not None:
        loss = full_loss

    return self.factor * loss.detach(), self.factor * kron

    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore a pickled backend.

    Pickles made before likelihood objects existed store the likelihood as a
    string under `likelihood`. It is turned into a likelihood object here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : dict[str, Any]
        the pickled `__dict__`.
    """
    state = dict(state)

    if "likelihood" in state:
        state["_likelihood"] = get_likelihood(state.pop("likelihood"))

    self.__dict__.pop("likelihood", None)
    self.__dict__.update(state)

    def _honours(self, method: str, y: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the library of this backend computes the curvature of `method`
    for the likelihood exactly.

    That is the case if the likelihood is exactly one of the `_library_types`,
    e.g. a `GaussianLikelihood` or a `CategoricalLikelihood`, whose losses the
    libraries know, and the library implements all of its non-default options. A
    subclass might override any member, e.g. `output_hessian`, which the library
    cannot see.

    With the targets `y`, the option `ignore_index` also counts as set if `y`
    holds ignored positions, even with the default `-100`. Libraries that don't
    honour it would count those positions, e.g. padding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"diag"`, `"kron"`, or `"full"`.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch.

    Returns
    -------
    honours : bool
    """
    if type(self.likelihood) not in self._library_types:
        return False

    options = set(self.likelihood.hyperparameters())

    if y is not None and _ignored_positions(self.likelihood, y) > 0:
        options.add("ignore_index")

    return options <= self._honoured_options(method)

    def _unsupported_error(
    self,
    method: str,
    honoured: frozenset[str] | None = None,
    stochastic: bool = False,
    y: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> ValueError:
    """Error for a curvature method that cannot handle the likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : str
        curvature method, e.g. `"kron"`.
    honoured : frozenset[str], optional
        options that the method honours, `_honoured_options(method)` by
        default.
    stochastic : bool, default=False
        whether the method computes a Monte Carlo Fisher.
    y : torch.Tensor, optional
        targets of the batch. If they hold ignored positions, `ignore_index`
        counts as an option, as in `_honours`.

    Returns
    -------
    error : ValueError
    """
    likelihood = self.likelihood

    if type(likelihood) in self._library_types:
        if honoured is None:
            honoured = self._honoured_options(method)

        options = set(likelihood.hyperparameters())

        if y is not None and _ignored_positions(likelihood, y) > 0:
            options.add("ignore_index")

        options = sorted(options - honoured)
        noun = "options" if len(options) > 1 else "option"
        what = f"the {noun} {', '.join(options)} of {likelihood!r}"
    else:
        what = f"the likelihood {likelihood!r}"

    where = f"{type(self).__name__}.{method}"

    if stochastic:
        where += " with stochastic=True"

    return ValueError(
        f"{where} does not support {what}. Use a deterministic GGN or EF "
        f"backend with the `diag` or `full` structure, which support any "
        f"likelihood."
    )

    _check_backward_hooks(full: bool) -> None

    Check that the model takes the kind of backward hooks the library uses.

    PyTorch refuses a module both regular and full backward hooks, and it remembers the kind of a hook after the hook is removed. ASDL registers regular hooks and leaves that mark on the model. BackPACK registers full ones, but its backends remove them and the mark after each computation.

    def _check_backward_hooks(self, full: bool) -> None:
    """Check that the model takes the kind of backward hooks the library uses.

    PyTorch refuses a module both regular and full backward hooks, and it
    remembers the kind of a hook after the hook is removed. ASDL registers
    regular hooks and leaves that mark on the model. BackPACK registers full
    ones, but its backends remove them and the mark after each computation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    full : bool
        whether the library registers full backward hooks.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        if a module of the model already had the other kind of backward hook.
    """
    clash = not full  # the flag PyTorch keeps for the other kind

    if not any(
        getattr(module, "_is_full_backward_hook", None) is clash
        for module in self._model.modules()
    ):
        return

    if full:
        what = "regular backward hooks, e.g. from fitting an ASDL backend"
    else:
        what = "full backward hooks, from `register_full_backward_hook`"

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"{type(self).__name__} can't use a model that had {what}. PyTorch "
        f"doesn't allow both kinds of backward hooks on one module, and it "
        f"remembers the kind after a hook is removed. Use a Curvlinops backend, "
        f"or a fresh instance of the model with the same weights, loaded with "
        f"`load_state_dict`."
    )

    def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using backpack's BatchGrad per output dimension. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, parameters, outputs)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        to_stack = []
        for i in range(model.output_size):
            model.zero_grad()
            out = model(x)
            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                if model.output_size > 1:
                    out[:, i].sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                else:
                    out.sum().backward(
                        create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                    )
                to_cat = []
                for param in model.parameters():
                    to_cat.append(param.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1))
                    delattr(param, "grad_batch")
                Jk = torch.cat(to_cat, dim=1)
                if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
                    Jk = Jk[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
            to_stack.append(Jk)
            if i == 0:
                f = out

        model.zero_grad()

    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad

    if model.output_size > 1:
        J = torch.stack(to_stack, dim=2).transpose(1, 2)
    else:
        J = Jk.unsqueeze(-1).transpose(1, 2)

    return (J, f) if enable_backprop else (J.detach(), f.detach())

    def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

    def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute selected output Jacobians using BackPACK's BatchGrad.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input data of shape `(batch, input_shape)` on the model's device.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    with self._extended(self.model) as model:
        columns = []
        first_output = None

        for column in range(outputs.shape[1]):
            model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            output = model(x)
            if first_output is None:
                first_output = output

            selected = output.gather(
                1, outputs[:, column : column + 1].to(output.device)
            ).sum()

            with backpack(BatchGrad()):
                selected.backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
                columns.append(
                    torch.cat(
                        [
                            parameter.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
                            for parameter in model.parameters()
                            if parameter.requires_grad
                        ],
                        dim=1,
                    )
                )
                for parameter in model.parameters():
                    if hasattr(parameter, "grad_batch"):
                        delattr(parameter, "grad_batch")

        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
            x.grad = input_grad

    result = torch.stack(columns, dim=1)
    assert first_output is not None

    return (
        (result, first_output)
        if enable_backprop
        else (
            result.detach(),
            first_output.detach(),
        )
    )

    def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at current parameter
    \\(\\theta\\) using Backpack's BatchGrad. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch, parameters)`
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    with self._extended():
        f = self.model(x)
        loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            loss.backward()
    Gs = torch.cat(
        [p.grad_batch.data.flatten(start_dim=1) for p in self._model.parameters()],
        dim=1,
    )
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
    return Gs, loss

    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)`
    y : torch.Tensor
        labels `(batch, label_shape)`

    Returns
    -------
    loss : torch.Tensor
    H_ef : torch.Tensor
        EF `(parameters, parameters)`
    """
    Gs, loss = self.gradients(x, y)
    Gs, loss = Gs.detach(), loss.detach()
    H_ef = torch.einsum("bp,bq->pq", Gs, Gs)
    return self.factor * loss.detach(), self._curvature_factor * H_ef

    _extended #

    _extended(module: Module | None = None) -> Iterator[Module]

    Extend module and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break torch.func and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind. Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    Parameters:

    • module (Module, default: None ) –

      module to extend, self._model by default.

    Yields:

    • module ( Module ) –

      the extended module.

    @contextmanager
def _extended(self, module: nn.Module | None = None) -> Iterator[nn.Module]:
    """Extend `module` and the loss with BackPACK for one computation.

    BackPACK's hooks stay on a module until they are removed, and they break
    `torch.func` and other backends on the same model. So the hooks are added
    here and removed on exit, together with the mark PyTorch keeps of their kind.
    Only the loss of a Gaussian or categorical likelihood is extended. BackPACK
    checks its options when it computes the curvature, after the fallback
    decision. Other likelihoods, e.g. the Bernoulli one, always fall back.

    Parameters
    ----------
    module : nn.Module, optional
        module to extend, `self._model` by default.

    Yields
    ------
    module : nn.Module
        the extended module.
    """
    module = self._model if module is None else module
    self._check_backward_hooks(full=True)

    modules = list(module.modules())
    kinds = [m._is_full_backward_hook for m in modules]
    lossfunc = (
        self.lossfunc if type(self.likelihood) in self._library_types else None
    )

    try:
        extend(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            extend(lossfunc)

        yield module
    finally:
        CTX.remove_hooks()
        _cleanup(module)

        if lossfunc is not None:
            _cleanup(lossfunc)

        for m, kind in zip(modules, kinds):
            m._is_full_backward_hook = kind

    def _flatten_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Flatten the targets to match the logits that are flattened to `(M, K)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : torch.Tensor
        outputs of the model for the batch, not flattened.
    y : torch.Tensor
        targets of the batch. For classification, class indices or class
        probabilities.

    Returns
    -------
    y : torch.Tensor
        `y` itself for regression, else `(M,)` class indices or `(M, K)` class
        probabilities, see `_flatten_categorical_targets`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        if the targets don't fit the outputs.
    """
    if self.likelihood.name == Likelihood.REGRESSION.name:
        return y

    self._check_targets(f, y)

    return _flatten_categorical_targets(f, y)

    def diag(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if not self._honours("diag", y):
        return super().diag(x, y, **kwargs)

    with self._extended():
        f = self.model(x)
        y = self._flatten_targets(f, y)
        # Assumes that the last dimension of f is of size outputs.
        f = (
            f
            if self.likelihood.name == Likelihood.REGRESSION.name
            else f.view(-1, f.size(-1))
        )
        loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
        with backpack(SumGradSquared()):
            loss.backward()
    diag_EF = torch.cat(
        [p.sum_grad_squared.data.flatten() for p in self._model.parameters()]
    )
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        diag_EF = diag_EF[self.subnetwork_indices]

    return self.factor * loss.detach(), self._curvature_factor * diag_EF

    kron #

    kron(
    x: Tensor | MutableMapping[str, Tensor | Any],
    y: Tensor,
    N: int,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any]
) -> tuple[Tensor, Kron]

    Compute a Kronecker factored curvature approximation (such as KFAC). The approximation to \(H\) takes the form of two Kronecker factors \(Q, H\), i.e., \(H \approx Q \otimes H\) for each Module in the neural network permitting such curvature. \(Q\) is quadratic in the input-dimension of a module \(p_{in} \times p_{in}\) and \(H\) in the output-dimension \(p_{out} \times p_{out}\).

    Parameters:

      total number of data points
